title: FBI Arrests Indian National Nitish Kaushal Days After Placing Him on Most Wanted List in Bhagwanpuria Crime Syndicate Case
excerpt: The arrest in Vermont is part of a sweeping federal prosecution of a Punjab-based transnational crime network that prosecutors say has over 1,000 members worldwide.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • FBI arrested Nitish Kaushal in Vermont after placing him on its Most Wanted list.
  • Kaushal is linked to the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria Organized Crime Group with over 1,000 members globally.
  • A 44-page indictment names 15 defendants, detailing the syndicate's international operations.
  • The arrest is part of Operation Hard Ball, targeting the Bhagwanpuria crime network.
  • FBI arrested Indian national Nitish Kaushal in Vermont, days after placing him on its Most Wanted list
  • Kaushal is charged with RICO conspiracy as part of the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria Organised Crime Group, which prosecutors say has over 1,000 members worldwide
  • A 44-page federal indictment names 15 defendants and alleges the Punjab-based syndicate operated across the US, Canada, UK, Europe, Australia and New Zealand
  • The arrest follows Operation Hard Ball, a multinational law enforcement offensive against the syndicate

The FBI has arrested Indian national Nitish Kaushal in Vermont, just days after placing him on its Most Wanted list, in a major development in one of the largest federal prosecutions targeting India-linked organized crime in the United States.

"Case Update: Nitish Kaushal has been arrested in Vermont," the FBI's Most Wanted account announced on X on Thursday. The bureau also appealed for public help locating "other fugitives wanted for committing crimes related to criminal enterprise investigations."

The Bhagwanpuria Crime Network

A 44-page federal indictment, obtained by IANS, alleges that the Jaggu Bhagwanpuria Organised Crime Group operated as a transnational criminal syndicate headquartered in India's Punjab state with members spanning six continents — the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, Europe, Australia and New Zealand.

Prosecutors allege the organization had more than 1,000 members and associates worldwide, including over 100 in the United States, and generated revenue through murder, kidnapping, drug trafficking, extortion, weapons trafficking, money laundering and human smuggling.

The indictment names 15 defendants, including alleged gang leader Jaggu Bhagwanpuria, Kaushal (who goes by the alias "Lala"), and several other alleged members.

Operation Hard Ball

Kaushal's arrest is part of Operation Hard Ball, a massive multinational law enforcement offensive designed to dismantle the Bhagwanpuria syndicate's global operations. The coordinated crackdown triggered synchronized raids and enforcement actions across the US, Canada and Europe.

A federal arrest warrant for Kaushal was issued on June 25 by the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California after a grand jury charged him with Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Conspiracy. Federal investigators allege Kaushal "carried out violent acts on behalf of the organisation, including kidnappings and assaults."

A Pattern of Crackdowns

The arrest adds to a growing list of FBI actions against India-linked criminal networks operating on American soil. The bureau also continues to seek Satinderjeet Singh, alias "Goldy Brar," who is wanted in connection with the Lawrence Bishnoi Organized Crime Group. A $50,000 reward has been offered for information leading to Singh's arrest.

These prosecutions represent a significant escalation in US law enforcement's engagement with transnational crime syndicates originating from South Asia. For the Indian diaspora in North America, the cases highlight how criminal networks exploit immigration corridors and diaspora communities to extend their reach.

Indian investigative agencies are cooperating with their American counterparts in these cases, marking a deepening of cross-border law enforcement collaboration between the two countries.
